reading.text: Every day, thousands of articles and posts appear online. Some of them are true, but many are rumors. How can you know? First, you must check the source. Is it an official website or a famous newspaper? Second, read more than the headline; some headlines are written only to get clicks. Third, look at the date; old news can spread again. Finally, compare the information with other sources. If you are not sure that something is a fact, you mustn't share it. Remember: fake news spreads faster than the truth.

reading.text: Many young people find it hard to save money. Here are some simple tips. First, write down your income and your expenses every month. If you know where your money goes, you will spend less. Second, don't buy things only because they are on sale. Ask yourself: "Do I really need it?" Third, save a small part of your income every month, even 10%. If you do this for a year, you'll have good savings. Finally, try not to borrow money; debt can cause stress and problems with friends.

reading.text: Fifty years ago, people communicated by letters and postcards. My grandfather remembers waiting weeks for a letter from his brother in Kuwait. Today, we can send a text in one second. We enjoy chatting with friends all over the world, and we can even see their faces in video calls. But some things haven't changed. Body language and tone are still very important. A message without emojis can sometimes sound angry. My grandfather says that a handwritten letter shows more love. Maybe he's right; I decided to write him one next week.

reading.en: Five Tips for Your First Job
reading.text: Are you going to look for your first job soon? Here are some tips. First, write a clear CV; one page is enough. Second, always send a short cover letter that explains why you want the position. Third, prepare for the interview: learn about the company and practice your answers. Fourth, be punctual and dress formally. Finally, if you don't have experience, take part in volunteer work or do an internship. Employers like ambitious and responsible candidates. Don't give up if you don't get the first job; every interview will teach you something.

reading.text: Every minute, millions of messages are sent and thousands of hours of video are uploaded. Social media platforms are used by billions of people. reading.en: Mesopotamia: The Land Between Two Rivers
reading.text: Iraq is often called the "cradle of civilization". Thousands of years ago, the Sumerians lived in the south, between the Tigris and the Euphrates. They invented writing, so we can read their stories today. They also built ziggurats and big cities like Ur. Later, King Hammurabi wrote one of the first sets of laws in Babylon. Although many of these cities are now ruins, their artifacts are in museums all over the world. However, the best place to see them is the Iraq Museum in Baghdad.

reading.text: In 2007, the Iraqi national football team did something that nobody expected. Although the country was going through very difficult times, the players were able to reach the final of the Asian Cup. Many of them couldn't train at home, so they practiced in other countries. reading.text: Today, we have more choices than ever. In the supermarket, there are fifty kinds of cereal, and online there are millions of videos. You might think that more options make us happier. However, scientists have found that too many choices can make decisions extremely difficult. People often hesitate, change their minds, and regret their choice afterwards. So what can we do? Experts suggest deciding what is important to you in advance, limiting your options to three, and making up your mind quickly. Remember: a good choice is better than a perfect one that never comes.

reading.text: For many years, people used to believe that our intelligence was fixed. However, scientists have discovered that the brain can change and grow. Every time you learn a new word, your brain builds new connections. If you practice it again and again, these connections become stronger. This is why consistency is more important than talent. People with a "growth mindset" believe that they can improve with effort. They don't give up when things are difficult; they bounce back and keep going. So remember: your brain is like a muscle. The more you use it, the stronger it becomes.
